fieldMarks: Usually reddish coat with white or ashy underparts.
Black lower legs ('stockings') and black-backed ears.
White tail tip, which distinguishes it from other foxes.
Colour phases include red, cross (about 25%) and silver or black (about 10%).
behavior: Mostly nocturnal or crepuscular and solitary, but territorial; families use a main earthen den.
Hunts rodents and rabbits with a high pounce; also eats birds, eggs, insects and plants.
Caches surplus food and revisits caches.
habitat: Highly adaptable: forest, tundra, prairie, desert, mountains, farmland and urban areas; favours broken country, marsh edges and hills.
range: Across Canada, Alaska and the United States. Introduced to some Alaskan islands through fox farming, and elsewhere to Australia.

lookalikes.name: Arctic fox
lookalikes.howToTell: Arctic foxes lack the white tail tip and are white or charcoal; red foxes dominate them where ranges overlap.

lookalikes.name: Gray fox
lookalikes.howToTell: Gray foxes have a black-striped, black-tipped tail and do not have black stockings.
